reasoning: According to historical records from the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and the Pew Research Center, the U.S. Congress has not passed all of its individual, regular appropriations bills on time (before the October 1 start of the fiscal year) since Fiscal Year 1997. For FY 1997, the final appropriations bills were enacted on September 30, 1996. Since then (FY 1998 to the present), Congress has consistently failed to meet the October 1 deadline for all of its federal spending bills, instead relying on Continuing Resolutions (CRs) to temporarily fund the government and subsequently passing omnibus packages or consolidated appropriations long after the fiscal year has started.
title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
